claim: This finding from the previous review no longer holds at the reviewed head: 1. The guard refuses a legal MySQL identifier that ends in a backslash. In `src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` the refusal at line 344 runs before the backtick test at line 345, so for a backtick-quoted identifier the backslash is never treated as data. I confirmed this at the reviewed commit: ``SELECT `a\` FROM t`` is refused with "MySQL backslash-escaped quotes are not allowed" under both the `mysql` dialect and no dialect, while sqlglot parses the same query to `Identifier(this='a\\', quoted=True)` with the identifier closing at the backtick. MySQL gives a backslash no special meaning inside a backtick identifier, so there is no boundary difference for the guard to protect against here, and the remedy the new documentation offers (doubled quotes) does not apply to this case. The failure is loud and fail-closed, so no unsafe query is admitted. No test covers a backtick identifier containing a backslash. (raised by 4/6 agents)
